senses.gloss:
Ūrjayant Aupamanyava is mentioned in the vaṃśa brāhmaṇa as a pupil of bhānumant aupamanyava.
Foot notes Indische Studien, 4, 372.

Ūrjayantī is regarded by Ludwig in one passage of the Rigveda as the name of a fort, the stronghold of nārmara. The verse is, however, quite unintelligible.
Foot notes Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 152.
ii. 13, 8.
Sāyaṇa makes Urjayantī a Piśācī; Grassmann, the sun; Roth, s.v. ūrjay, takes it adjectivally. Cf. Oldenberg, ṛgveda-Noten, 1, 199.

Ūrjavya, a word occurring only once in the Rigveda, is taken by Ludwig to be the name of a sacrificer. Roth, however, regards the word as an adjective meaning ‘rich in strength,’ and this is the more probable interpretation.
Foot notes v. 41, 20.
Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 155.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
